alert.alert.title: Alert
alert.alert.text:
A detection that arrived from outside: a SIEM, EDR or other tool posting to the alerts API (for example through n8n), or an e-mail turned into an alert by a mail rule. Each alert belongs to one customer, and only users with access to that customer (and administrators) can see or work it.

An alert is triaged here, then closed, or escalated or merged into a case. When it arrives it may be grouped into an alert cluster by a clustering rule and get investigation-flow checklists attached.

alert.filters.title: Alert filters
alert.filters.text:
Every field you fill in must match. Title, description, source and tags match any part of the text, ignoring case; source reference matches any part but is case-sensitive. Asset(s) name, IOC(s) and Alert(s) ID take exact values, separated by commas without spaces. A date range applies only when both its start and end dates are set.

The filter is kept in the page address, so a copied link reproduces the same view.

alert.search.title: Searching alerts
alert.search.text:
Type conditions in the search bar and press Enter; each becomes a chip you can remove or click to edit. Conditions side by side must all match; OR joins everything before it with everything after it, NOT or a leading - excludes, and brackets group. The server reads the search, so a mistake is reported with what is wrong.

A word on its own searches the title, description, source, source reference and tags. Press / anywhere on the page to jump to the bar.

items.name: is:open / is:closed
items.text: Open means not Closed, Merged or Escalated.

items.name: status, severity, customer, classification, resolution, owner
items.text: By name, in quotes if it holds a space. owner:me is whoever is searching; owner:none and resolution:none are the empty ones. Severity also compares: severity:>=High.

items.name: title, description, source, ref, note
items.text: Contains the text. An unquoted * or ? makes it a wildcard over the whole value: title:phish*.

items.name: tag, asset, ioc
items.text: An exact tag; or any attached asset's name or IOC's value containing the text.

items.name: created, event_time
items.text: A day (created:2026-10-01), a comparison (created:>=2026-10-01), or a range: created:[2026-10-01 TO 2026-10-31]. Times are UTC.

items.name: id, case, cluster
items.text: An alert ID, a linked case ID, a cluster ID (cluster:none is an alert in no cluster).

alert.views.title: Alert views
alert.views.text: The page remembers your choice in this browser.

items.name: List
items.text: One line per alert across the page; opening one replaces the list with its details, and Back returns.

items.name: Split
items.text: The queue with the selected alert beside it. Drag the divider to resize the queue.

items.name: Board
items.text: Open alerts in columns: unassigned ones by severity, or assigned ones by status. Dragging a card to another column changes that severity or status; Take assigns the alert to you.

alert.queue_clusters.title: Clusters in the queue
alert.queue_clusters.text: Alerts grouped by a clustering rule appear as one expandable row, with how many of them match the search; only the matching ones are listed, and pages count these rows. Open goes to the cluster's own page. When a filter names alert IDs or a cluster, the alerts are listed one by one.

alert.new_alert.title: New alert
alert.new_alert.text: Raise an alert by hand, for anything that did not come in through a feed: a hotline call, an out-of-band report. It goes through the same steps as an ingested alert, so clustering rules and investigation flows apply to it.

alert.keyboard.title: Keyboard triage
alert.keyboard.text: With no text box in focus, in List and Split:

items.name: j / k
items.text: Next and previous alert.

items.name: Enter / Esc
items.text: In List, open the selected alert's details and close them again.

items.name: e
items.text: Escalate the selected alert to a new case.

items.name: m
items.text: Merge it into an existing case.

items.name: x
items.text: Add it to or remove it from the selection for batch actions.
Jump to the search bar.

alert.source.title: Alert source
alert.source.text:
The name of the tool or feed that raised the alert, as the sender wrote it (a SIEM or EDR name, for example). Alerts created by a mail rule carry the rule's source label, Mail by default.

It is used for filtering, by clustering rules and investigation flows (field alert_source), and as the source of the timeline event when the alert is added to a case timeline.

alert.source_reference.title: Source reference
alert.source_reference.text: The alert's identifier in the system that raised it (a ticket, event or detection ID), so the original can be found there. Alerts created from e-mail carry the message's Message-ID. The filter matches any part of it, case-sensitively.

alert.source_event_time.title: Source event time
alert.source_event_time.text:
When the detected activity happened, according to the source, shown in UTC. The alert list is sorted by this time (newest first unless you flip the order), and it becomes the date of the timeline event when the alert is added to a case timeline. Alerts created from e-mail use the message's Date header.

It can differ from the IRIS creation time, which is when IRIS-NG received the alert.

alert.creation_time.title: IRIS creation time
alert.creation_time.text: When IRIS-NG received and stored the alert, in UTC. Alert-cluster windows are measured on this time rather than on the source event time, because events can arrive late or out of order.

alert.owner.title: Alert owner
alert.owner.text:
The analyst responsible for triaging the alert. Assigning someone else notifies them (according to their notification settings). Assign to me takes the alert yourself; Unassigned in the filter finds alerts nobody owns.

Changing anything on an alert that has no owner (its status, note or resolution, for example) makes you its owner. With several alerts selected, only the unowned ones become yours; alerts that already have an owner keep them, and an owner picked with Assign goes to every selected alert.

alert.custom_conditions.title: Custom conditions
alert.custom_conditions.text:
Extra filter conditions written as JSON: a list of {"field", "operator", "value"} objects, which must all match together with the fields above. A field is an alert column (alert_title, alert_severity_id, alert_tags...) or a related field written relation.column (severity.severity_name, status.status_name, customer.name). The panel shows an example to copy.

A field that does not exist makes the search fail. This is not the grammar used by clustering rules and investigation flows.

items.name: eq / not
items.text: Equal to / different from the value.

items.name: in / not_in
items.text: One of / none of the values; the value is a list, for example [1, 2].

items.name: like
items.text: Contains the value anywhere, ignoring case.

alert.saved_filters.title: Saved filters
alert.saved_filters.text: Save filter (in the Filter panel) stores the panel's fields, custom conditions included, and the search bar under a name; pick it later from Saved filters to apply it again. A private filter is listed only for you. A shared one is listed for every user, and any user can delete it.

alert.linked_cases.title: Linked cases
alert.linked_cases.text:
The cases an alert was escalated or merged into, shown as #number links at the bottom of the alert; the Case ID filter finds the alerts linked to one case. Closing a linked case closes its alerts too, with a resolution matching the case outcome.

Unlinking an alert from a case removes only the link: the IOCs, assets and timeline event already copied into the case stay, and the alert's status does not change.

alert.escalate_merge.title: Escalate or merge into a case
alert.escalate_merge.text: Moves the alert into a case. The IOCs and assets you tick are copied into the case, the case tags are added, your note goes into the case summary, and the alert keeps a link to the case. Escalating a single alert into a new case notifies its owner, if that is someone else.

items.name: Merge into a new case
items.text: Escalates: creates an Open case for the alert's customer, with its classification, a link back to the alert in the summary and the chosen case template. A single alert also gives the case its severity and description and becomes Escalated; when several selected alerts go into one new case, each becomes Merged.

items.name: Merge into existing case
items.text: Adds the alert to a case you can access and adds a line naming it to the case summary. The alert becomes Merged. Nothing is copied again for an alert already linked to that case.

alert.import_iocs_assets.title: IOCs and assets to import
alert.import_iocs_assets.text: The alert's IOCs and assets, all ticked by default. Ticked items are copied into the case; unticked ones stay on the alert only. An IOC the case already has (the same normalised value and type) is linked instead of being added twice. Imported assets start with an unspecified analysis status.

alert.escalation_note.title: Escalation note
alert.escalation_note.text: Free text added to the case summary under an Escalation note heading, for example why the alert was escalated. When several alerts go into a case at once, the note is added once.

alert.import_as_event.title: Alerts as timeline events
alert.import_as_event.text: Adds one event per alert to the case timeline: titled [ALERT] and the alert title, dated at the alert's source event time, with the alert description as content, the raw alert as raw data and the imported IOCs and assets linked. The events are marked to appear in the graph and the summary; flag, edit or delete them like any other event.

alert.case_template.title: Case template
alert.case_template.text: Applies a case template to the new case: its title prefix is put in front of the case title, its summary text is appended to the case summary, and its tags, tasks and note directories are added. Templates are managed on the Case Templates page. Merging into an existing case applies no template.

alert.template_suggestion.title: AI case-template suggestion
alert.template_suggestion.text:
When the dialog opens for a single alert, the AI backend reads the alert (title, description, source, severity, classification, tags and up to 20 IOCs and 20 assets) with the list of case templates, preselects the template it judges the best fit and shows its confidence and reason. Choosing another template dismisses the suggestion.

It is only a preselection: nothing is created until you confirm, and the suggestion is not saved. It is not offered when several alerts are escalated together.

alert.close_with_note.title: Close with note
alert.close_with_note.text:
Closes the alert (status Closed) and records, in the same step, its resolution, note and tags. Setting the status to Closed from the status menu changes the status only; setting another status reopens a closed alert.

With several alerts selected, they all get the same resolution, and the note you enter replaces each one's note.

alert.alert_note.title: Alert note
alert.alert_note.text: A free-text note kept on the alert itself, shown on its Notes tab. Saving replaces the previous note (the alert history records that it changed). It is not copied into a case when the alert is escalated; use the escalation note for that.

alert.relationships.title: Alert relationships
alert.relationships.text: A graph of other alerts of the same customer that share an asset (same name and type) or an IOC (same value and type) with this one, and of that customer's cases containing those values. It is computed automatically and is an indication, not a confirmed link.

items.name: Show open / closed alerts
items.text: Open means New, Assigned, In progress, Pending or Unspecified; closed means Closed, Merged or Escalated.

items.name: Show open / closed cases
items.text: Adds the customer's open or closed cases that contain the shared IOC values or asset names.

items.name: Nodes limit
items.text: Caps how many related entries are fetched (100 by default).

items.name: Lookback (days)
items.text: Only alerts received within that many days are considered (180 by default).

alert.context.title: Alert context
alert.context.text: Free-form key and value details the sender attached to the alert (host names, user names, detection rule names...). Alerts created from e-mail carry the sender, recipients, subject, Message-ID, folder and the name of the mail rule that matched. Clustering rules and investigation flows can match on these as alert_context.<key>.

alert.raw_alert.title: Raw alert
alert.raw_alert.text: The original alert content as the source sent it, stored unchanged; for alerts created from e-mail, the headers and the first 4 KB of the body. When the alert is added to a case timeline it becomes the event's raw data. Clustering rules and investigation flows can match on it as alert_source_content.<path>.

alert.enrichment.title: Enrichment
alert.enrichment.text: Extra data (JSON) supplied with an IOC or asset through the API, for example by the workflow or module that sent the alert. IRIS-NG stores and shows it; it does not act on it.
